questions.prompt: You are designing a run to test whether your own pipeline is position-sensitive. In the multi-document QA design, what is the one thing that changes between two runs, what is held fixed, and what does that discipline let you conclude from a difference in accuracy?

With the relevant document placed in the middle of the input, GPT-3.5-Turbo's multi-document QA accuracy fell past a particular reference point. What was that reference point, what was its value, and why is falling below it worse than merely a drop in accuracy?

A model fails a multi-document QA item and also fails a key-value retrieval item. What explanation is still open in the first case that the second case rules out, and what property of the key-value inputs rules it out?

Query-aware contextualization was measured on both tasks in the Lost in the Middle paper. What did it do to each one, and what should you conclude before applying a mitigation that was validated only on a synthetic probe?

The U-shaped attention pattern was re-measured after randomly shuffling the document order. What would a content-driven bias have done under that shuffle, what actually happened, and what does the result establish?

One paper measures a U-shaped attention bias in two 7B models; another argues the behaviour follows from causal masking and residual connections. How do the two claims differ in scope, and how would you go about checking each one?

Someone proposes reranking the best passage into the first slot as a universal fix for position effects. Which two findings from this chapter argue against treating that as universal, and what does each one show?
